why: The owner's first hands-on review disagrees with the reviewers on the cases he named, which means the loop optimises a rubric that misses what he judges. n35 scored 85, the highest of cycle 9 (docs/v3/cycles/expression-9.md:55-58): he says 'kind of nice idea but horrible rendering, looks poorly designed'. n15 scored 80 and passed first try (expression-6.md): 'too much screaming blue, choose colour only where expression needs it'; both of its series are accent blues (apps/playground/src/demo/series.ts:139-141) and the reviewer rubric allows 'the primary data series' as an accent site with no count (packages/basalt-ui/agent/reviewer/rubric.md:44), while the skill's 'one accent' is prose only (agent/skills/basalt-design/references/charts.md:22, encoding.md:19, SKILL.md:14). n32 passed at 81: 'looks weird'. n04 was never marked for a hover that makes the plot jump. n02 and n04 were never marked for ink-weight row rules. n27 never passed (70 to 76) and his note is about form: a grid of chart cards that should offer a table view. His overall verdict is still 'we are on the right path'. An earlier owner review produced X1 to X5 (expression cycle 2); this is the second calibration and it should land the same way.
what: docs/v3/expression/rubric.md, packages/basalt-ui/agent/reviewer/rubric.md, the basalt-design and basalt-charts skill references, docs/v3/EXPRESSION.md where it names the calibration set, and a calibration record.
must_not_touch: docs/v3/cycles/** (past cycle pages stay as scored)
change: (1) Record the review verbatim in docs/v3/expression/calibration-owner-2.md with the owner's words per case (in this brief's `owner_words`), the round scores those cases got, and the gap. (2) Add or sharpen rubric items so each remark has a line a reviewer must score from the shots: a colour budget (accent on at most one series or one mark class per view, counted, with the rest in ink steps; a second accent needs a stated second meaning); separator weight (a rule between rows is at most the grid token, never ink); craft of hand-composed marks (alignment to a shared grid, label fit, no clipped or hidden titles, consistent mark sizes) scored separately from the idea, so a good idea drawn badly cannot pass; layout stability under hover (the lead tool's sweep frames must show the plot at one position); form choice for many small cards (a card grid of records offers a table view). Weight them so n35, n15 and n32 as shipped would fail: rescore those three and n04 from their existing last-round shots with fresh reviewers and put the scores in the calibration page. If the rescored cases still pass, the items are too weak. (3) Skill: turn the same lines into instructions with a self-check the builder runs before shooting (count accent series; no bare border; hover sweep), and say where the owner's preference came from. (4) Where a rule can be a lint rule rather than prose, name it in the PR for the lead of v3-owner-1-row-rules or as a follow-up; do not write package code here.
